issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Developer instance method named attend(course:), but the solution's Developer implementation provides a method named participateIn(course:). This name mismatch between the solution and the specified API will confuse students about the correct method to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across artifacts. Rename the solution's participateIn(course:) method to attend(course:) so it matches the problem statement and template, or alternatively rename the template/problem references to participateIn if that name is preferred. Ensure all references (including examples and tests) use the same method name.

issues.description: Within the solution repository there is an internal inconsistency: Client.swift calls myself.attend(course:), but Developer.swift defines participateIn(course:). This mismatch will prevent the solution from compiling and misleads students about the correct API to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution self-consistent: either (A) rename Developer.swift's participateIn(course:) method to attend(course:) so Client.swift's call compiles, or (B) change Client.swift to call participateIn(course:) instead of attend(course:). Prefer option (A) to match the problem statement and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template ask students to implement a Developer method named attend(course:), but the solution implements the same functionality under a different method name participateIn(course:). Additionally, the solution's Client calls attend(course:), creating an internal mismatch. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (a developer attending a course) will confuse students mapping the requirement to the implementation and may cause compilation or usage errors when following the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Rename the solution method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) (or vice versa, and update the problem statement and template accordingly). Preferably change the solution Developer implementation to define func attend(course: Course?) { ... } so it matches the problem statement, the template stub, and the Client call.
